articles.description: 'Until Hormuz fully re-opens and confidence returns, the crude reality is that pressure at both ends of the barrel will intensify', Aramco Chief Executive Amin Nasser said.

articles.description: Ithaca Energy agreed to buy Suncor Energy's stakes in oil projects offshore Newfoundland and Labrador for up to $1.11 billion.

articles.title: USA Continues Strategic Petroleum Reserve Release
articles.description: 'The United States continues to lead the coordinated efforts to stabilize oil markets for the benefit of Americans and people around the world', U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said.

articles.title: Indian State Firm BPCL Readies $3-Billion Bond to Fund Brazil oil Project
articles.description: Indian state-owned refiner Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) prepares to issue a $3-billion bond to finance its share of a major offshore oil development in Brazil, as Indian companies move to expand in international upstream to secure crude oil supplies. BPCL, India’s second-largest state-controlled oil refiner, expects to raise the sum via several tranches and has held roadshows in London, Singapore, and Dubai to assess potential investor interest, anonymous sources with knowledge of the plan told Bloomberg on Monday. articles.title: Buru Launches Approval Process for Western Australian Gas Project
articles.description: Buru referred the Rafael Gas Project to Western Australia's Environmental Protection Authority, which will open a comment period before deciding to assess the proposed development onshore the Canning Basin.

articles.title: OPEC+ 7 Reveal Production Plan for November
articles.description: A statement posted on OPEC's website revealed Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria, and Oman's production plan for next month.

articles.title: Namibia approves Eco’s farm-down of three offshore licences to bp
articles.description: Offshore exploration company Eco (Atlantic) Oil & Gas has obtained the final regulatory clearance needed to complete its farm-down of a 60% stake in three Namibian exploration licences to BP.

articles.title: Possible Fire Reported at Saudi Refinery as Attack Claims Circulate
articles.description: Reports of a possible attack on Saudi Arabia's Petro Rabigh refining and petrochemical complex north of Jeddah emerged on Monday, although Saudi authorities have so far not confirmed that an attack took place. Iran's Tasnim news agency, citing Yemeni sources, reported that an oil refinery in the Jeddah area had been attacked. So far, Tasnim appears to be the primary source for the specific claim of an attack, with no confirmation from Saudi authorities or Saudi Aramco. There are, however, indications that a fire has occurred at the facility. Videos…

articles.title: EU Electric Vehicle Sales Hit Record as Fuel Prices Surge
articles.description: Record-high fuel prices and a record number of newly available affordable models have pushed electric vehicle sales in the European Union to an all-time high this year, Transport & Environment, a European advocacy group for clean transport and energy, said in a report on Monday. Between January and August, sales of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) soared by 45% from a year earlier to as many as 1.64 million units across the EU. In a landmark achievement, BEVs outsold gasoline-fueled cars for the first time over a full quarter in the second…

articles.title: Petrobras reports new oil discovery in Amapá block FZA-M-59
articles.description: Petrobras has announced the discovery of a new oil-bearing interval in the Morpho well, located in ultra-deep water block FZA-M-59 off the coast of the Brazilian state of Amapá.

articles.title: Supreme Court Takes Up Boulder Climate Suit Against Exxon and Suncor
articles.description: Today, the U.S. Supreme Court will hear arguments about whether a lawsuit filed in state court in Colorado seeking damages from two major oil companies for the climate-change related damage inflicted on Boulder County can go forward. Here's the short version: The Canadian-based Suncor Energy Inc. and Texas-based ExxonMobil say that policies regarding climate change and any alleged damages resulting from it are matters for the federal government and courts only and that therefore the state suit should not be allowed to go forward. articles.title: Aramco CEO Warns Oil Inventories Are ‘Scarily Thin’
articles.description: Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser warned Monday that the world has lost nearly 3 billion barrels of gross oil supply since the Iran war began, equivalent to roughly half the crude and products that normally would have moved through the Strait of Hormuz over the same period, leaving global inventories “scarily thin” even as crude flows from the Middle East recover. The world entered the crisis with almost 10 billion barrels of oil stocks, according to Nasser, but more than 1 billion barrels have since been drawn from inventories to offset…

articles.title: Rubio Opens 4-Day NATO Tour in Iceland to Discuss Arctic Security
articles.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is heading to Iceland, Greece, and Portugal on October 5-8 for talks on security, defense, energy, economic cooperation, and technology as NATO allies face growing security concerns over Russia’s military activity and continued Middle East instability. Rubio will begin in Reykjavik, where he is expected to discuss Arctic security and economic cooperation with Icelandic officials. He will then travel to Athens for the sixth US-Greece Strategic Dialogue, with defense cooperation, energy, regional security,…

articles.title: Houthis Claim Strike on Aramco Facility in Riyadh as Yemen Fighting Escalates
articles.description: Despite reports of surging oil flows out of the Strait of Hormuz, tensions in the Middle East remain high as the fresh Saudi-Houthi escalation threatens to unravel recent success in restoring oil exports. This weekend, the Iran-aligned Houthis claimed a missile and drone attack on a facility of Saudi Aramco in Riyadh, the Saudi capital city. articles.title: Iran Oil Minister Quits as Exports Dry Up
articles.description: Iran's Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad resigned citing personal reasons, as the Islamic Republic tries to sustain its oil industry under a tightening U.S. blockade.

articles.title: Suncor to sell east coast offshore stakes in Canada to Ithaca for $860m
articles.description: Suncor Energy has agreed to divest its stakes in three East Coast offshore assets in Canada to Ithaca Energy for C$1.2bn ($860m) in upfront cash.

articles.title: South Korea Plans to Triple Canadian Crude Imports as Saudi Share Slips
articles.description: The share of Saudi crude in South Korea’s oil imports dipped below 30% for the first time since 2021, as the resource-poor G7 economy moved to diversify supplies amid the Middle East crisis. In the period January to August, Saudi crude oil accounted for 29.9% of total South Korean crude imports, local news agency Yonhap reported on Monday, citing data from Korea National Oil Corp. and the Korea Petroleum Association. Saudi Arabia has remained South Korea’s top crude oil supplier despite the slump in its share of total imports, which…

articles.title: Japan Rules Out More Reserve Releases After G7 Pledges 100 Million Barrels
articles.description: Japan does not plan to carry out additional releases of crude oil from its national reserves, a senior government official said on Monday, even as the G7 group announced on Friday a 100-million-barrel release from stocks. “Japan has been releasing oil from reserves for some time now and there are no plans for a further release at this stage,” Minoru Kihara, Japan’s chief cabinet secretary, said on Monday, as carried by Reuters. Japan is a member of the G7 group of the world’s most industrialized nations, which pledged on…

articles.title: Hormuz LNG Flows Still Down More Than 75% Despite Rebound
articles.description: LNG traffic at the Strait of Hormuz appears to be ticking up despite increased threats to shipments in the chokepoint in recent days. At least three LNG carriers have transited the Strait of Hormuz outbound since the end of last week, tanker-traffic data compiled by Bloomberg and Kpler showed on Monday. The increase in LNG shipments extends the rebound in transits in September, but the flows of liquefied natural gas remain over 75% below the levels seen before the Iran war. articles.title: Diesel Margins Slide as G7 Announces 100 Million Barrel Stocks Release
articles.description: The G7 announcement of a release of 100 million barrels of crude oil and diesel has pressured down middle distillate refinery margins, which had hit record highs last month. The start of stock releases over the next four months and the reduced risk of a U.S. ban on diesel exports sent the ICE gasoil crack down to about $70 per barrel now, from as high as $85 a barrel in the middle of last week, Warren Patterson, Head of Commodities Strategy at ING, said on in a note on Monday. articles.title: Aramco Cuts Asia Oil Prices to Six-Year Low, Raises Prices for Europe
articles.description: Saudi Aramco has raised oil prices for European-bound cargoes in November but has cut prices for Asian buyers to the lowest in six years, Reuters reported today, noting analysts had expected price hikes. According to the pricing information, Aramco will be offering Arab Light at a discount of $5 per barrel to the Dubai/Oman benchmark for Asian buyers next month. The cut amounted to $3 per barrel and is the lowest since June 2020, according to Reuters records. For European buyers, on the other hand, the November oil price will be $3 per barrel higher…
